claims.text: Pack cementation with aluminum oxide can improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention is pack cementation with aluminum oxide.
Pack cementation produces an aluminum oxide surface layer.
The aluminum oxide surface layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the aluminum oxide layer reduces oxidation of the alloy.
At 1000°C in air for 100 hours, the treated alloy will have an oxidation rate at least 50% lower than that of the untreated alloy.
The intervention is expected to work over 900–1100°C in air.
The intervention is expected to work over 900–1100°C in an inert gas.
The effectiveness of the aluminum oxide layer may depend on the specific refractory high-entropy alloy composition.
The effectiveness of the aluminum oxide layer may depend on the pack-cementation process parameters.
Oxidation rates and aluminum oxide layer thicknesses will be measured after exposing treated and untreated alloys at 1000°C in air for 100 hours.
The hypothesis is falsified if the treated alloy's oxidation rate is not at least 50% lower than that of the untreated alloy.
